Articulate 360 Block Runtime
nodes.rationale: Articulate/Storyline SCORM content climbs window.parent looking for a real SCORM API and would otherwise write lesson_status/score/suspend_data straight to the LMS, colliding with this module's own completion tracking (Storyline could mark the module 'completed' the moment its own last slide passes, even if the learner is still early in this module). artMakeShim intentionally walls off all SCORM calls from embedded Articulate packages: only student_name/student_id are read through (never written back); everything else (lesson_status, suspend_data, quiz score) is redirected to a block-scoped localStorage key via artStoreKey/artLoadCmi/artSaveCmi and never reaches the LMS. Articulate's own suspend_data can run tens of KB, far past SCORM 1.2's ~4096-char cmi.suspend_data limit, which is the other reason it can't be folded into this module's own state. window.API/API_1484_11 are only installed when HAS_ART is true, so modules without Articulate content never gain a fake SCORM object on window.

nodes.label: SCORM API Wrapper
nodes.rationale: Auto-detects SCORM 1.2 (window.API) or SCORM 2004 (window.API_1484_11) by walking the window/parent/opener chain. Explicitly skips any API object flagged __modulShim so that once the Articulate shim (artMakeShim) is installed on window.API, this module's own scormFindAPI does not mistake its own shim for the real LMS API and fail to find the genuine one further up the chain.

Learner Activity Tracking
nodes.rationale: Writes activity events directly to Supabase (not through SCORM cmi.suspend_data, which is capped ~4096 chars and would silently truncate per-slide duration data for long modules). The anon key is visible in shipped source by design: Supabase RLS grants the anon role INSERT-only, zero SELECT, so the key cannot be used to read other learners' data (see server/supabase_activity_setup.sql).

nodes.label: Activity Outbox Retry Queue
nodes.rationale: A training runs once: a learner who has finished won't reopen the module, so a lost activity batch never gets a second chance to send. Failed batches persist to localStorage (not memory, since the most common failure mode is the tab being closed) and are retried on the next flush - including from a different module opened later, since all modules share one browser origin. HTTP 4xx responses are treated as a permanent rejection (schema/RLS misconfiguration) and the batch is dropped; 429/5xx are treated as transient and requeued.

nodes.label: Learning Recap Popup ('Ringkasan Belajarmu')
nodes.rationale: Deliberately framed as a personal mirror of the learner's own session, not a report card, per Self-Determination Theory (Deci & Ryan, 1985/2000): motivation driven by external control/evaluation undermines intrinsic motivation. Accordingly the popup shows no final score, no ranking, and no comparison of the learner's name against other participants; the underlying numbers come from the backend endpoint /api/activity/my-recap, but the narration sentences are composed client-side so wording can change with a re-export instead of a backend redeploy.

nodes.label: Video Progress Tracking
Identity Resolution & NIP Capture
nodes.rationale: NIP is the sole cross-module identity key; a learner accepted with a name but no NIP would fragment into an unlinkable '(no identity)' bucket in Command Center, so identity is only auto-accepted when a NIP is present. Resolution order: state already saved in this module -> full SCORM identity (has NIP) -> cross-module shared-identity cache (has NIP) -> manual form (SCORM name, if any, only prefills the form). SCORM-reported IDs are not assumed to be a NIP (LMS internal IDs vary), so each session records identity_source to distinguish manually entered NIPs from LMS-supplied IDs during analysis.

nodes.label: Reading-Speed & Idle Detection
nodes.rationale: The 4-minute idle threshold (ACT_IDLE_MS) is a deliberately loose estimate of 'learner stepped away', chosen as a middle ground between productivity-tool defaults (~3-5 min) and news-site scroll-tracking thresholds (~5s); it is added ON TOP OF each slide's own Brysbaert-derived minimum reading time (238 wpm, SLIDE_MIN_MS) via actIdleThresholdMs(), not used in place of it. Bug fixed 2026-08-02: before actIdleThresholdMs() existed, every slide used a flat 4-minute idle cap, which could both mislabel an attentive reader on a long slide as 'abandoned' in Command Center and falsely trigger the rushed-reading warning (which compares active time against 50% of SLIDE_MIN_MS) because activeMs was cut off before the real reading time was reached.
